elements.label: Show Customer Reviews On A Dish
elements.hint: A star rating, the reviews left so far, and a form to add one. New reviews are held until you approve them under Comments & Reviews — a customer whose order contains the dish is published straight away and shown as a verified buyer. Shown only while Enable Comments is on under Settings → Application → Interactions & Sharing, which governs the whole storefront

elements.label: Menu Layout
elements.hint: Grid suits photographed dishes; list suits long menus. A Menu Sections block set to Theme default follows this

elements.label: Dishes Per Row (Desktop)
elements.hint: Ignored when the layout is set to list. A Menu Sections block set to Theme default follows this

elements.label: Dish Image Ratio
elements.hint: Applied to every dish card so a mixed-aspect photo set still lines up

elements.label: Show Prices On Dish Cards
elements.hint: Turn off for a menu priced only on the dish page. Any Menu Sections or Dish Grid block set to Theme default follows this

elements.label: Show Tags As Badges
elements.hint: Spicy, New, Halal, Vegan — read from the dish's tags. Blocks set to Theme default follow this

elements.label: Show Short Description
elements.hint: One clamped line under the dish name. Blocks set to Theme default follow this

elements.label: Sticky Section Navigation
elements.hint: Pin the menu-section jump links while the customer scrolls

elements.label: Saved Dishes
elements.hint: One switch for the whole feature: the heart on every dish card and dish sheet, the header link, and the Saved Dishes page. Saved dishes live in the customer's own browser, so they do not follow them to another device

elements.label: Quick View
elements.hint: A magnifier on every dish card that opens a closer look — every photograph, the full description and the labels — without leaving the menu. It does not replace the dish page: a dish with sizes or a compulsory question is still answered there

elements.label: Comments On Stories
elements.hint: Readers may comment on a blog post. Every comment from someone without an account is held until you read it, under Comments & Reviews — a story has no order to check them against. Shown only while Enable Comments is on under Settings → Application → Interactions & Sharing, which governs the whole storefront

elements.label: Likes On Stories
elements.hint: A heart with a count on each blog post. Shown only while Comments On Stories is on, and while Enable Likes is on under Settings → Application → Interactions & Sharing

elements.name: Ordering Modes
elements.subtitle: What you offer is configured in core now — Sales → Shipping. Create a Pickup-type shipping method per branch to offer collection; delivery zones and their methods price the delivery leg. The settings below shape how ordering behaves once offered.

elements.label: Pickup Ready Wording
elements.placeholder: e.g. Ready to collect in about 20 min
elements.hint: Shown to a customer who chooses pickup, in place of the delivery address form
elements.default: Ready to collect in about 20 minutes

elements.label: Minimum Order — Delivery
elements.hint: Refused below this, before the delivery fee is added — which is how customers read a minimum. Leave empty for no minimum

elements.label: Minimum Order — Pickup
elements.hint: Usually empty: a customer collecting costs you no delivery, so most shops set no minimum for it

elements.label: Collection Address
elements.hint: Where the customer comes to collect. Shown on the cart the moment they choose pickup — leave it empty and the shop's footer address is used instead

elements.label: Offer Dine In
elements.hint: Adds a third choice beside Delivery and Pickup, and asks which table. The order is still handled as a collection — no address, no delivery fee — so the kitchen sees DINE IN and the table instead of PICKUP. This is the shop-wide switch and it is no longer the whole answer: each branch also has its own Offers Dine In (Saffron → Outlets → the branch → The dining room), which starts OFF. With branches, this switch permits dining and each branch decides whether it seats anybody

elements.label: How Many Tables
elements.hint: The FALLBACK, used only by a branch that has listed no tables of its own. List the tables on the branch instead (Saffron → Outlets → the branch → The dining room): this one number gives every branch the same room, so a shop whose branches differ will offer tables that do not exist at one of them. Leave both empty and the customer types whatever their table is called

elements.label: Ask About Cutlery
elements.hint: Puts an opt-out on the cart — the customer says they do not need it, and the kitchen sees NO CUTLERY on the ticket. Off by default: a shop that always packs cutlery should not ask a question it will ignore

elements.name: Table Bookings
elements.subtitle: Everything about reserving a table lives here — how long a booking holds its table, and how far ahead one may be made. Set the shop's defaults below and override them per branch only where a branch genuinely differs; these figures are configured nowhere else. Today is never bookable: a table booked for later can never be in dispute with somebody who has just sat down, which is what keeps the floor manageable.

elements.label: Accept Table Bookings
elements.hint: OFF (the default) means dine-in is for customers already sitting down: they are not offered a time at all. Turn it ON to take reservations — a booked table is really held, inside the order's own transaction, so a second party cannot be given the same table at the same time. Today is never bookable; today's diners are walk-ins

elements.label: How Long A Booking Holds A Table
elements.hint: Minutes, counted from the booked time. The table is unavailable to anyone else for this long, so this decides how many sittings an evening holds: 60 turns a table twice between 7 and 9, 120 once

elements.label: Earliest A Table Can Be Booked
elements.hint: Days ahead. 1 means the soonest bookable table is tomorrow — today is never bookable, so everyone dining today is a walk-in and the floor is never juggling reservations against people already sitting down. 2 gives the kitchen a day's notice

create.title: Branch Booking Length
create.subtitle: Only for a branch that genuinely differs — a dining room that turns once an evening beside a café that turns three times. Every other branch uses the default above.

elements.label: Holds The Table For (Minutes)
elements.hint: Leave empty to use the shop default above

elements.label: Earliest Booking (Days Ahead)
elements.hint: This branch alone — a kitchen that preps a day earlier than the others needs 2 where the shop says 1. Leave empty to use the shop default above

elements.label: Prep Time Wording
elements.hint: Shown wherever an ASAP order is described

elements.label: Sold Out Wording
elements.hint: Shown on the dish card and the dish sheet when a dish — or every size of it — has stock 0. A Dish Sheet block can override it

elements.label: Closed Shop Message
elements.placeholder: e.g. We're closed right now — browse the menu and order when we open at 11am.
elements.hint: Shown on the storefront while you are closed, and returned to anyone who tries to order then. Say when you reopen — a holiday's own Reason wins for its date
elements.default: We're closed right now — browse the menu and we'll take your order when we reopen.

elements.name: Scheduled Ordering
elements.subtitle: Let a customer pick when they want their order instead of as soon as possible. The times offered come from your Service Hours, so a closed day never appears.

elements.label: Offer A Time Picker At Checkout
elements.hint: Off means every order is as soon as possible — and is then refused whenever you are closed, since there is no slot to choose instead. On, the chosen time is shown to the kitchen and checked against that day's hours

elements.label: How Many Days Ahead
elements.hint: Today counts as the first day. Anything from 1 to 365 — 90 is three months, 180 is six, 365 is a year. The next seven days are one-tap buttons; past that the customer picks a date from a calendar, up to this limit. Set it to what your kitchen can actually plan for: an order taken for six months out is priced from today's menu and paid for today, and it waits under Booked Ahead on the Kitchen Queue until its week comes round

elements.name: Kitchen Alerts
elements.subtitle: Whether the Kitchen Queue speaks up when an order arrives. The screen refreshes itself either way — this decides whether anybody in the room finds out without looking at it.

elements.label: Announce New Orders
elements.hint: On, a new order raises a message on the Kitchen Queue and sounds a chime. Off, the screen still refreshes but says nothing — right for a shop that watches the tablet, wrong for a busy pass

elements.label: How Insistent
elements.hint: How many times the chime sounds for one arrival. Two is right for most kitchens; three for a loud pass. Silent still shows the on-screen message, for a counter in a quiet dining room

items.title: Silent — show it on screen only
